assertions.text: Tests use @Test(arguments:) parameterised cases — not one test function per case, and not a loop over cases inside a single test body.
Test function bodies contain no for/while loops or forEach — cases are supplied via @Test(arguments:), not iterated manually.
Test function bodies contain no if/switch/guard branching — expected outcomes come from the argument rows, not branching logic.

Each case reads as a coherent row pairing input with expected outcome — labelled tuple elements, a row struct, or zip of collections — not multiple independent collections passed to arguments: (which Swift Testing combines as a cartesian product) and not parallel arrays indexed manually.

Every fee tier is represented (free, 50%, 80%, full value) and every boundary is tested from both sides: 30 days (free) vs 29 days (50%), 7 days (50%) vs 6 days (80%), 1 day (80%) vs 0 days (full value). Middle-tier boundaries (7/6 and 1/0) must not be skipped in favour of only the outer edges.
The started-stay case is expressed as its own test using #expect(throws:) — not mixed into the fee table via sentinel values, optional expectations, or branching inside the test body.

Case values are concrete domain values (days like 29, fees like 100 for a 200-euro booking) — not abstract placeholders, computed expressions like bookingValue / 2, or symbolic constants that hide the actual numbers from the reader.
